name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
remarks: This module simulates the progression of Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) from onset through treatment phases.
Models age-dependent subtypes, genetic mutations, and treatment responses.
Based on WHO classification, ELN risk stratification, and modern treatment protocols.
Age is classified at the moment of each annual onset check (Age_Risk_Assessment,
invoked every pass of AML_Development_Monitoring), not once at whatever age
(1-10 years, via the old birth-rolled Initial_Delay) the person happened to be
when the module first ran. The pre-fix module set aml_patient_type exactly once
and never revisited it, so a person who survived past 18 or 60 kept accruing AML
risk at pediatric rates forever ('pediatric forever' bug) and adult-onset AML was
never generated. Adult annual incidence (1e-5 <60y, 8e-5 60y+) approximates the
~10x rise with age reported in Shallis RM, Wang R, Davidoff A, Ma X, Zeidan AM.
'Epidemiology of acute myeloid leukemia: Recent progress and enduring challenges.'
Blood Rev. 2019;36:70-87 (age-adjusted incidence 2.0/100,000 <65y vs 20.1/100,000
65y+); this module's own values are lower in absolute terms (controller-specified)
but preserve the same ~8x steep age gradient using this module's pre-existing
60-year adult-subtype threshold rather than 65.
Rapid_AML_Progression (a Death state) was structurally present but never wired
into any reachable relapse path, so no simulated patient ever died of AML --
relapsed/refractory patients cycled through salvage therapy and response
reassessment forever ('immortal relapsing disease' bug). Relapse_Mortality_Check
now gates entry to each salvage round at a per-relapse-event death probability
derived from post-relapse survival data (see its own remarks).
Congenital/infantile AML (including transient myeloproliferative disorder
progressing to AML) presents at or shortly after birth -- unlike the
pre-fix module, which rolled this same 2e-05 chance at whatever birth-rolled
age (1-10 years) Initial_Delay happened to land on.
Rate unchanged from the pre-fix module (2e-05); out of this task's explicit
numeric scope, which specifies only the recurring pediatric/adult annual
rates below. Retained as a distinct, near-birth, high-risk pathway.
Re-invoked every AML_Development_Monitoring pass (annually) so
aml_patient_type always reflects the person's CURRENT age, not a value
frozen at first classification. The three age bands are exhaustive and
mutually exclusive over all non-negative ages, so no fallback branch
is needed.
1e-05/yr, ages 18-59 -- controller-specified calibration; see module-level
remarks for the real-world age-gradient citation.
8e-05/yr, ages 60+ -- controller-specified calibration; see module-level
remarks for the real-world age-gradient citation.
Annual reroll (was 3-12 months, which both inflated per-pass hazard and
made annual rates awkward to apply cleanly). direct_transition to
Age_Risk_Assessment on every pass is the core 'age classification at
diagnosis, not once' fix: whichever age band the person is CURRENTLY in
gets re-evaluated and re-set every single pass.
The pre-fix module fired Azacitidine_Administration and Transfusion_Support
with no encounter open at all on this path (AML_Diagnosis_End had already
closed the diagnosis encounter, and AML_Treatment_Pathway -- itself only
reachable by looping back through Azacitidine_Administration/Transfusion_
Support/AML_Diagnosis_End every induction pass -- opened nothing new).
Verified by a (state, encounter_open) BFS: Azacitidine_Administration,
Transfusion_Support and AML_Diagnosis_End were each reachable in BOTH the
encounter-open context (first, correct, pass through the diagnosis
encounter) and the encounter-closed context (every subsequent induction
loop pass). This encounter, opened once per induction course, removes the
closed-context path entirely.
~21-35 day inpatient length of stay for induction chemotherapy and count
recovery -- a legitimate carve-out under the inpatient encounter-lock rule
(< 90 days), matching the ~28-day pattern already established for ALL
induction in this tree (commit 6dd9df2b). Named to avoid the *_Supply_Delay
idiom, which the linter always treats as CRITICAL while an encounter is open
regardless of legitimacy.
Response_Assessment (and therefore Complete_Remission) is reachable from
Supportive_Care, which never sets venetoclax_therapy. The pre-fix module
called Venetoclax_End (referenced_by_attribute: venetoclax_therapy)
unconditionally, which NPEs at State$MedicationEnd.process
(State.java:1623, 'medication.stop' on a null attribute lookup) and drops
the whole patient record -- one of the 22 MedicationEnd-on-unset-attribute
states found by the tree-wide static check in task 1.10's report (S3/S9),
which names this module explicitly. This guard skips straight to
Surveillance for anyone who never started venetoclax.
Rapid_AML_Progression (a Death state) existed in the pre-fix module but was
reachable only through an attribute-guarded branch of the old
AML_Development_Monitoring complex_transition that could never be true in
practice (aml_stage only ever reaches 1 after the person has already left
the monitoring loop for good) -- confirmed unreachable by transition-target
analysis, not by the naive structural BFS (which cannot see attribute-guard
semantics and reports it as reachable). No simulated AML patient could ever
die of AML; relapsed/refractory disease cycled through salvage and
reassessment forever.
0.20 per relapse event approximates published post-relapse survival:
Breems DA, Van Putten WL, Huijgens PC, et al. 'Prognostic Index for Adult
Patients With Acute Myeloid Leukemia After First Relapse.' J Clin Oncol.
2005;23(9):1969-1978 (2-year OS after relapse 4.7%-46% by risk group); and
DiNardo CD, Wei AH. 'How I treat acute myeloid leukemia in the era of new
drugs.' Blood. 2020;135(2):85-96 (relapsed/refractory AML median OS well
under 12 months without transplant). Combined with this loop's reused
60/20/20 Response_Assessment split (each relapse round: 20% die before
reassessment, 48% of the original cohort reach CR, 32% loop again), the
finite-absorption cumulative mortality among relapsed patients is
0.20/(0.20+0.48) = 29.4% -- directionally correct (relapsed AML carries a
real risk of death that the pre-fix module modelled as zero) but likely
still optimistic relative to the ~10% real-world 5-year OS after relapse,
because Response_Assessment's 60% CR rate (realistic for FRONTLINE
induction) is reused unmodified for salvage rounds, where real CR rates are
considerably lower. Recalibrating Response_Assessment for salvage specifically
is out of this task's scope; noted as a follow-up concern.
The pre-fix module ordered this med (chronic: true, 28-day prescription)
and then immediately called MedicationEnd on it at the same instant, with
no elapsed time and no encounter -- a chronic medication that starts and
stops simultaneously, and a same-instant response reassessment straight
after a relapse diagnosis. This delay gives the salvage cycle real
duration (1-2 28-day cycles) before MedicationEnd and reassessment,
matching VIALE-A-era venetoclax + hypomethylating-agent response-
assessment timing (first assessment at end of cycle 1, confirmed by
cycle 2-3).
